mcqs.question: What is the time period (T) of an oscillation?

options.A: The time taken for one complete oscillation.
options.B: The number of oscillations that occur in one second.
options.C: The maximum displacement from the equilibrium position.
options.D: The force required to start the motion.

mcqs.answer: The time taken for one complete oscillation.
mcqs.explanation: The time period, denoted by T, is defined as the duration of one full cycle of the motion. Option B describes frequency, C describes amplitude, and D is unrelated.

mcqs.question: Frequency (f) of a periodic motion is defined as:

options.A: The time taken for one complete oscillation.
options.B: The number of complete oscillations per unit time.
options.C: The maximum distance from the mean position.
options.D: The restoring force acting on the system.

mcqs.answer: The number of complete oscillations per unit time.
mcqs.explanation: Frequency measures how many cycles occur each second (or other time unit). Option A is the definition of period, C is amplitude, and D is unrelated to frequency.

mcqs.question: Which statement correctly defines periodic motion?

options.A: Motion that repeats itself at regular time intervals.
options.B: Motion that occurs only once and never repeats.
options.C: Motion that has a constant speed but changing direction.
options.D: Motion that requires an external force to continue.

mcqs.answer: Motion that repeats itself at regular time intervals.
mcqs.explanation: Periodic motion is characterized by repetition after a fixed time interval (the period). Options B, C, and D describe other types of motion and are not definitions of periodic motion.

mcqs.question: A child on a swing moves back and forth repeatedly about the lowest point of the swing. Which term best describes this motion?
mcqs.explanation: The swing moves repeatedly about an equilibrium (lowest) position, which is the hallmark of oscillatory motion. Linear, rotational, and projectile motions are different categories.

mcqs.question: A mass is attached to a vertical spring. When the mass is released, it oscillates up and down. Which point represents the equilibrium position of the system?

options.A: The highest point reached by the mass during oscillation.
options.B: The lowest point reached by the mass during oscillation.
options.C: The point where the spring is neither stretched nor compressed.
options.D: The point where the net force on the mass is zero.

mcqs.answer: The point where the net force on the mass is zero.
mcqs.explanation: Equilibrium occurs where the restoring force of the spring balances the weight, making the net force zero. Option C would be true only for a horizontal spring without gravity; in a vertical setup the equilibrium is where forces cancel, not necessarily where the spring is unstretched.

mcqs.question: A simple pendulum is pulled aside to a maximum angular displacement of 15° and then released. What is the amplitude of this oscillation?

options.B: The time taken for one complete swing.
options.C: The number of swings per minute.
options.D: The force required to pull the pendulum.

mcqs.explanation: Amplitude is the maximum displacement from the equilibrium position; for a pendulum it is the greatest angular deviation. Options B and C refer to period and frequency, while D is unrelated.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements about the time period (T) of an oscillation is correct?

options.A: T is the same as the frequency of the motion.
options.B: T is the reciprocal of the frequency.
options.C: T is the maximum speed reached during oscillation.
options.D: T is the distance traveled in one complete cycle.

mcqs.answer: T is the reciprocal of the frequency.
mcqs.explanation: Time period T = 1/f, where f is frequency. Option A confuses the two quantities, C describes maximum speed, and D confuses distance with time.

mcqs.question: If the time period of a pendulum is 0.5 s, what is its frequency and why?

options.A: 2 Hz, because frequency is the reciprocal of the period.
options.B: 0.5 Hz, because frequency equals the period.
options.C: 1 Hz, because one oscillation occurs every second.
options.D: 4 Hz, because frequency is four times the period.

mcqs.answer: 2 Hz, because frequency is the reciprocal of the period.
mcqs.explanation: Frequency f = 1/T. With T = 0.5 s, f = 1 / 0.5 = 2 Hz. Options B, C, and D misuse the relationship between period and frequency.
